title: Buffered queue
hints: `len` and `cap` work on channels: `len(ch)` is how many values are waiting in the buffer, `cap(ch)` is the buffer size. Since only one goroutine uses the queue, checking them first tells you whether a send or receive would block.

`New` stores `make(chan string, capacity)`. A send on a buffered channel blocks only when it is full, so `Push` returns `false` when `len(q.ch) == cap(q.ch)` and otherwise sends. `Pop` returns `"", false` when `len(q.ch) == 0` and otherwise receives.

`Push`: `if len(q.ch) == cap(q.ch) { return false }; q.ch <- s; return true`. `Pop`: `if len(q.ch) == 0 { return "", false }; return <-q.ch, true`. `Len` and `Cap` are one line each. With capacity 0, `len == cap == 0`, so `Push` always says full.
